summary: Dave Richard's CBSSports.com Week 5 2023 Fantasy Football column goes game by game with starts, sits, sleepers and busts, backed by matchup stats, film notes and defensive tendencies. It covers Jaguars-Bills, Texans-Falcons, Ravens-Steelers, Panthers-Lions, Saints-Patriots, Giants-Dolphins, Titans-Colts, Bengals-Cardinals, Eagles-Rams, Chiefs-Vikings, Jets-Broncos, Cowboys-49ers, Packers-Raiders and Bears-Commanders. Key calls include sitting Dameon Pierce, Tank Dell, Miles Sanders and Russell Wilson, and starting DeAndre Hopkins, Garrett Wilson, Jordan Love and Terry McLaurin.
one_line: Dave Richard's Week 5 2023 Fantasy Football guide gives start/sit, sleeper and bust advice for each NFL game with matchup data.
key_facts: Trevor Lawrence is called a dicey start at Buffalo (BUF -5.5, O/U 48.5): he has completed just 50% of third-down throws and has an EPA per dropback of minus-0.72 under pressure.
Bills cornerback Tre'Davious White tore his Achilles and edge rusher Greg Rousseau won't play, weakening Buffalo's pass rush, which has a 38.2% pressure rate with a 15.3% blitz rate.
Gabe Davis is a boom/bust flex: 16.8 ADOT but a 13.6% target share, with a touchdown in three straight games.
Dameon Pierce and Tank Dell are sits at Atlanta; the Falcons have not allowed more than 8 non-PPR/11 PPR points to any running back, and Dell had zero deep targets last week.
Jonnu Smith is a sneaky sleeper over Kyle Pitts at TE for Falcons-Texans; Arthur Smith said Pitts isn't at 100%, and Houston allows an 84% catch rate to tight ends.
Najee Harris has zero touchdowns and just one carry inside the 15-yard line; Pittsburgh has run the second-fewest red-zone plays (18).
Miles Sanders' snap share hit a season-low 43% and his yards per carry fell from 4.0 to 1.5 over four games; the Lions allow 2.9 yards per rush to running backs.
Raheem Mostert is a bust candidate vs. the Giants after two fumbles, as De'Von Achane played all but two snaps inside the 10-yard line over two weeks.
DeAndre Hopkins is a start vs. the Colts, who lost cornerback Dallis Flowers to a torn Achilles and lead the NFL in missed tackles on passing plays with 10.
Joe Burrow is a mild sleeper at Arizona: the Cardinals have the league's lowest blitz rate (14%), but Burrow has just two touchdown passes and is 2 for 22 on throws of 15-plus Air Yards.
Russell Wilson is a sit vs. the Jets, who have the third-best pressure rate (41.6%) and allowed over 16 Fantasy points to a quarterback only once, while Denver's line allows a 39.5% pressure rate.
Garrett Wilson is a start vs. Denver, which allows an 85.1% catch rate to wide receivers; 11 of his 36 targets from Zach Wilson were uncatchable.
Brock Purdy is a sit vs. Dallas, which leads the league in pass rush pressure rate (55.6%) even without Trevon Diggs; Purdy has hit 20 Fantasy points in 8 of 9 regular-season starts.
Sam Howell is a sleeper vs. the Bears, who allow a 70.1% completion rate, and Terry McLaurin is a start since every top outside receiver has scored at least 10 PPR points against Chicago.
